# Component

# Page Component

This provides an abstraction for the concept of a page. One benefit it has is that it's hooked up with additional lifecycle callbacks should you need to leverage on it for logic.All components being registered to the`IPageRegistry`in the implementation of [ISeaTalkApplication](/docs/rn-sdk/application)should subclass from this.

# Lifecycle

![](data:image/png;base64,)

|Lifecycle|Description|
|---|---|
|pageBecameReady|This will be after componentDidMount and will be invoked when the page has become fully visible to the user for the first time.|
|pageBecameHidden|Triggering conditions: 1. Pushing a new page on top and thus the current page has become hidden 2. When app goes to background, the current page will also receive the event|
|pageBecameUnhidden|Triggering conditions: 1. When all the pages on top has been popped and the current page has thus become visible again. 2. When app goes from background back to foreground the top most page will also receive this event.|
|pageBecamePartiallyHidden|This will be called when a new page has been pushed in a way that does not fully blocked the current page. NOTE: This will NOT be triggered when pushing a native page. (e.g. when showing an alert)|
|pageReceivedData|This will be called when the top page has popped itself and pass back some data.|

# Page Insets

PageComponent supports the concept of page insets, which correspond to native view's insets. In order to facilitate this, we introduce an interface called SafeAreaInsets, detailed below:

```javascript
export interface SafeAreaInsets {
    top: number;
    bottom: number;
    left: number;
    right: number;
} Copy
```

There are two ways to access the page's insets:

1. *(property*) pageInsets: SafeAreaInsets
2. This property represents the current insets
3. pageInsetsDidChange(newInsets: SafeAreaInsets)
4. This method can be overridden to be notified for any changes to the page's insets

# SafeAreaView

This is a wrapper component to handle SafeArea for iOS.

```javascript
render() {
    return (
        <SafeAreaView><Text> {this.props.title} </Text></SafeAreaView>
    )
} Copy
```

# Image

## Usage

You can use`<imgae/>`to display an image in your RN App just like in a normal web page.

```javascript
<Image
    source={{ uri: 'https://reactjs.org/logo-og.png' }}
    style={{ width: 400, height: 400 }}
/> Copy
```

## Handling images using cache data

In SeaTalk RN, we will use a different cache strategy from the [original React Native cache strategy](https://reactnative.dev/docs/images#cache-control-ios-only)when caching images for display. The most significant difference is that SeaTalk will**use disk instead of RAM**to store the cache data.You can specify the cache stragety you want to use in the following format

```javascript
<Image
    source={{
        uri: 'https://reactjs.org/logo-og.png',
        cache: 'reload',
    }}
    style={{ width: 400, height: 400 }}
/> Copy
```

Possible values for`cache`

|Value|Cache Stragety|
|---|---|
|default|The data for the URL will be loaded from the existing cache data in disk.|
|reload|The data for the URL will be loaded from the originating source. No existing cache data should be used to satisfy a URL load request.|
|force-cache|The existing cached data will be used to satisfy the request, regardless of its age or expiration date. If there is no existing data in the cache corresponding the request, the data is loaded from the originating source.|
|only-if-cached|Different from vanilla React Native, we do not support this one|
